en: Marcela Agoncillo sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong, not in the Philippines, before it was raised during the 1898 Declaration of Independence.
The Philippine Senate consists of only twenty-four elected senators, making it one of the smallest upper legislative houses in the entire world.
National hero Jose Rizal was a brilliant polymath who could speak and write in twenty-two different languages, including Spanish, Latin, and Japanese.
The indigenous Ifugao people carved the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces over two thousand years ago using only simple hand tools and no modern machinery.
Before the Spanish arrived, early Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an ancient alphabetic writing system with seventeen distinct characters.
The vibrant Ati-Atihan festival in Aklan is known as the mother of all Philippine festivals because it inspired the creation of Sinulog and Dinagyang.
In 1955, Filipino scientist Dr. Gregorio Zara successfully invented and demonstrated a working video telephone prototype, decades before the technology became commercially available.
Juan Luna won the first gold medal for the Philippines at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884 for his massive painting Spoliarium.
The President of the Philippines can only serve a single six-year term and is strictly prohibited by the Constitution from running for re-election.
The formal Philippine national costume for men, the barong tagalog, is traditionally woven from delicate, translucent fibers extracted directly from pineapple leaves.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it.
Andres Bonifacio founded the Katipunan, a secret revolutionary society that initiated the Philippine Revolution using a traditional blood compact called the sandugo.
